races.name: Racedays For 9 Pound At Nottingham Racecourse Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Ivor Thirst Sprint Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Gold Star Gallop Handicap

runners_data.name: Charlie Boyo
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's 3yo has a live second on good ground at 5f but is a genuine hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield map slot; the step up to 6f is a slight query and racing without his natural backmarking position tempers expectations, though Georgia Dobie's claim helps on the weights.

runners_data.name: Duskaura
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's form is solid (13/61 in 14 days) and Duskaura placed fourth on good ground last time, but this is a sprinter whose natural inclination is to race from behind — operating in midfield rather than the rear alters the rhythm she typically needs to produce her best.

runners_data.name: Macanudo
runners_data.note: Ian Williams has only one winner from 47 runners over the past 14 days, and this 5yo's recent form has all been over 7f on standard-paced surfaces; the drop to 6f on good-to-firm is a concern, and being pushed up from his preferred backmarking position adds further complication.

runners_data.name: Eartha
runners_data.note: Richard Fahey's 2yo filly returns after 351 days off — by far the longest layoff in this field — with all her form gathered on good or softer ground; the quick surface may not be an issue based on her best run, but race-fitness after almost a year away is a genuine flag, especially with a 5lb apprentice taking off the claim.

runners_data.name: Acclaimed Freedom
runners_data.note: George Scott's 3yo showed a win and a place in recent starts and is the most straightforward hold-up horse in the field without a redistribution flag; form includes a win on standard ground and a second on soft, and Rowan Scott's partnership with the trainer is worth noting in a competitive handicap.

runners_data.name: Zarinca
runners_data.note: The key pace figure — Edward Bethell's 3yo won over course and distance on standard ground and is confirmed as the sole front-runner; Paul Mulrennan takes the ride and the uncontested lead on quick going over a straight six puts Zarinca in an ideal tactical position, though her style fit note flags she may be racing outside of a pure pacemaking role.

runners_data.name: Emperor Caradoc
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's 7yo is the course-form specialist in this field, with three course wins and consistent recent efforts at 6f on good ground; David Nolan keeps the ride, and Emperor Caradoc's past headgear (p) suggests he needs galvanising — if he settles kindly he represents the most credible hold-up threat to Zarinca.

runners_data.name: Beyond Borders
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost have no winners from 14 runners in the past fortnight, and this 5yo's best recent form includes a win on standard ground and a second on good; a natural hold-up operator remapped to midfield, he is suited by a fast surface but his trainer's current form is a lukewarm angle.

races.paceDynamic: Zarinca is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner 6f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Nottingham, and with no other genuine pace horse to challenge her, she is set to dictate a controlled, unchallenged tempo from the gate. That uncontested lead on fast ground over a straight six furlongs creates a classic front-runner's platform — sustainable fractions, minimal energy expenditure, and the ability to quicken again approaching the final furlong if needed. The field is packed with hold-up horses — Charlie Boyo, Duskaura, Macanudo, Eartha, Beyond Borders and Acclaimed Freedom all prefer to race off the pace — meaning the closers will need a meaningful late burst to bridge the gap Zarinca establishes. This shape decisively favours prominent and front-running profiles; hold-up horses face a significant task in a genuinely steady-to-honest solo-led race on a surface where ground is riding quicker than the declared going suggests. Note that the field contains far more hold-up types than can realistically be deployed at the rear without interference, with Beyond Borders, Charlie Boyo and Duskaura among those who may find themselves shuffled further forward than preferred, though none is likely to challenge Zarinca for the lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zarinca Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Zarinca leads uncontested and the pace is honest but manageable, enabling her to quicken entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Zarinca leads uncontested and the pace is honest but manageable, enabling her to quicken entering the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Close Late
scenarios.trigger: If Zarinca sets an overly strong gallop that leaves her vulnerable in the final furlong, allowing the closers to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: If Zarinca sets an overly strong gallop that leaves her vulnerable in the final furlong, allowing the closers to finish powerfully.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Zarinca Overpresses, Midfield Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Zarinca's early pace proves unsustainable and horses tracking in mid-division get a clean run to the line.
scenarios.body: If Zarinca's early pace proves unsustainable and horses tracking in mid-division get a clean run to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Burst
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a falsely slow tempo that bunches the field and produces a sprint finish off a weak gallop.
scenarios.body: If the race is run at a falsely slow tempo that bunches the field and produces a sprint finish off a weak gallop.

watchPoints.text: Watch Zarinca's early strides — if she establishes a clear uncontested lead by the 5f pole, the front-running scenario becomes near-certain and hold-up horses will struggle to close on this quick ground.

Emperor Caradoc wore a hood (p) and has form figures that fluctuate sharply; if he races freely early or fails to settle, his late effort will be compromised and he will not perform the hold-up role that makes him relevant to the finish.

Eartha's 351-day absence is the most significant fitness concern in the race — watch the market closely for any drifting that suggests connections are not confident she is fully wound up after her layoff.

Beyond Borders and Charlie Boyo are both genuine hold-up horses operating out of their natural position; if either overcomes the redistribution and finds a clean run wide entering the final furlong, they are capable of posting a late run that looks faster than the pace shape would suggest.

The going is riding good-to-firm for this 7:00 race based on the course report — faster than the declared good — which will shorten finishing times and further reward Zarinca's economy of effort at the head of affairs.

races.name: Nottingham's Finest Ale Mile Handicap

runners_data.name: Jack Langley
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here and will get a soft lead on Good to Firm; his sim-going record of 1 win from 4 places suits these conditions and Rowan Scott should simply control fractions, though his STYLE_FIT flag suggests he's being asked to operate fractionally outside his sharpest zone, and a 7-day turnaround keeps him fresh.

runners_data.name: Saratoga Gold
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost's eight-year-old has a consistent placed record over 1m4f-1m6f on similar going including two placed efforts at 16f, and with a 24-day freshen-up he should travel smoothly in behind Langley; a genuine hold-up type who can legitimately track the pace in this small field without being displaced.

runners_data.name: Free World
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' five-year-old carries a worrying finishing trend — the fades-in-finish warning is backed by a recent form string of 4/9-09 — and while shown in midfield due to redistribution, his true inclination is to sit deepest of all; the small field means he cannot find the cover he needs, and that is a significant tactical problem on a day when pace is limited.

runners_data.name: Ikigai Star
runners_data.note: 309 days off the track is the dominant headline here — a long absence accompanied by a visor and a 53-jump hurdles detour — though Charlie Longsdon's horse has a solid placed record over 18-21f in good ground and the step back to 1m6f on a flat track is a straightforward enough test if fitness is there.

runners_data.name: Chambers
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's four-year-old returns after 222 days (31 jumping days), winless in flat handicaps across five recent attempts with finishes clustering around fifth to seventh; a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield on the map because of the crowded rear, where his out-of-role position further undermines what is already a thin flat form profile.

runners_data.name: Regally Blonde
runners_data.note: Ben Case's seven-year-old has cheekpieces fitted and arrives 33 days fresh, but a form string of 07-756 and a sim-going record of 2 wins from 10 efforts over 12-16f signals inconsistency; like Free World and Chambers, his natural hold-up instincts are squeezed by the field composition, and the style displacement compounds the already modest recent evidence.

races.paceDynamic: Jack Langley is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no meaningful pressure expected from the rest of the field, he is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over 1m6f on Good to Firm ground at Nottingham. The six hold-up types behind him — including Saratoga Gold, Ikigai Star, and the redistributed Free World, Chambers, and Regally Blonde — will track him at varying distances, but none are naturally drawn to chase him hard early, meaning fractions are unlikely to be punishing. The race shape strongly favours a horse capable of travelling smoothly in behind a slow-to-moderate pace and producing a sustained finish, rather than one reliant on a strong gallop to get cover or use up early; closers who need genuine pace to aim at will be left cold. Three runners — Free World, Chambers, and Regally Blonde — are genuine hold-up horses whose natural positions at the rear cannot all be accommodated in such a small field, and it is Saratoga Gold and Ikigai Star who are best placed to secure the tracking berths closest to Langley.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Langley Controls, Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Jack Langley leads at a steady tempo and the hold-up horses who genuinely track him closest make their move in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Jack Langley leads at a steady tempo and the hold-up horses who genuinely track him closest make their move in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Langley increases tempo significantly after halfway and none of the hold-up types can close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: If Langley increases tempo significantly after halfway and none of the hold-up types can close the gap in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Stormer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early but then lifts sharply, creating a sprint finish that suits a horse finishing hard from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely slow early but then lifts sharply, creating a sprint finish that suits a horse finishing hard from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Finish, Chaos Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace causes the field to bunch dangerously in the straight, leading to interference or positional trouble that scrambles the expected outcome.
scenarios.body: If the steady pace causes the field to bunch dangerously in the straight, leading to interference or positional trouble that scrambles the expected outcome.

watchPoints.text: Jack Langley controls all variables here — if he bowls along unchallenged and Rowan Scott dictates a truly slow tempo, the bunching effect in the straight could make him very hard to pass.
Ikigai Star's 309-day absence (including 53 jumping days) is a serious fitness flag — watch the market for any drift that suggests connections are not fully confident about her readiness.

Free World is flagged as fading in finishes and is genuinely displaced from his preferred deep hold-up berth; if he fails to get cover early, Paul Mulrennan may have to ride him more aggressively than his style demands, compounding the risk.

Saratoga Gold's three placed efforts at 1m6f-2m in similar going make him the most experienced trip-and-conditions horse in the field — watch how quickly William Pyle positions him to track Langley, as securing that second-slot berth could be decisive.

With three horses (Free World, Chambers, Regally Blonde) all naturally wanting to sit deepest but unable to all do so in a six-runner field, watch the early positioning battle for signs of horses racing uncomfortably wide or covering more ground than ideal.

races.name: Shipstones 1852 Heritage Cup Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Celestias Comet
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up filly with James Fanshawe maintaining a quiet 3-from-14 record over the past fortnight; best form on Good ground suits today's Good to Firm conditions but she has not won in 9 similar-going runs, making her a place prospect rather than a win banker at 1m2f.

runners_data.name: Phaedra
runners_data.note: Connections ship her over from South Africa having placed twice in 15 similar-going starts, and Tom Kiely-Marshall claims 5lb which helps at the weights; her two-from-four placed record on Good turf and a recent 8-day turnaround after a 10f run on Good suggest freshness is there, and she profiles as one of the more straightforward hold-up types who could travel smoothly into contention.

runners_data.name: Huggable
runners_data.note: JF Egan takes the ride on a filly whose natural inclination is to race from the rear, though the positional congestion in this field has seen her mapped to midfield — she is not a true tracker and that context should temper confidence; on Good ground she has placed twice in ten attempts and her 9-from-10f Nottingham run is not encouraging, though the step to 1m2f is a plausible trip upgrade.

runners_data.name: Saliko
runners_data.note: Rowan Scott partners this filly who carries a prominent-going tag despite her redistribution to the front; she is the de facto pace-setter today and her 4-from-10f Good ground form includes a win, but her role as sole leader in an unfamiliar front-running slot introduces uncertainty — a STYLE_FIT score of 0.80 signals meaningful discount if the race shape demands she sustains the lead all the way.

runners_data.name: Rosemary May
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby has saddled 14 winners from 112 in the last 14 days and Rhys Elliott claims 5lb for the pilot; the key concern is a clear finishing warning flagged in her profile — she fades in the finish — which is a serious liability in a steady-run race where the winner will likely need to sustain an effort all the way to the line, and her redistribution to midfield from a true hold-up style compounds the stylistic mismatch.

runners_data.name: Dinah Myte
runners_data.note: John Gallagher's filly arrives on the back of a win (1/8f/STA) just 19 days ago and holds a 2-from-6 current trainer strike rate; she has raced exclusively up to 10f and today's 1m2f is a career-longest trip, while the step to Good to Firm ground from her Tapeta and Fibresand wins raises an unresolved question about surface preference — true hold-up type shuffled into midfield by the field's structural shape.

races.paceDynamic: Saliko is the lone confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the front from a hold-up tag, meaning this 1m2f contest on Good to Firm ground at Nottingham will be run at a measured, sustainable gallop with no genuine rival prepared to push for the lead. With Huggable, Rosemary May, and Dinah Myte all true hold-up types compressed into midfield due to the field's positional congestion, there is meaningful pace in the race but it will not translate into a hot early tempo — Saliko can control the fractions entirely on her own terms. The result is a race likely run at an even, unhurried clip that sets up for a one-paced finish rather than a true late sprint, benefiting horses with the tactical speed to travel prominently or to pick off a lone front-runner who has not been pressured. Closers' chances are structurally undermined here: several of the horses mapped to midfield are redistribution products, not natural hold-up horses who thrive on a genuine end-to-end gallop, so the race shape favours any runner who can sit just off Saliko's shoulder and pounce in the straight without needing a true strong pace to run into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Saliko Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Saliko bowls along at a comfortable solo gallop and the field is content to track without applying any pressure through the first mile.
scenarios.body: If Saliko bowls along at a comfortable solo gallop and the field is content to track without applying any pressure through the first mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong and the true hold-up types — despite being mapped to midfield — manage to find a genuine strong gallop to run into in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: If the pace is surprisingly strong and the true hold-up types — despite being mapped to midfield — manage to find a genuine strong gallop to run into in the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at an even enough tempo that one of the redistributed midfield runners manages to pick off a fading Saliko from a tracking position approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the race is run at an even enough tempo that one of the redistributed midfield runners manages to pick off a fading Saliko from a tracking position approaching the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Tactically
scenarios.trigger: If early confusion over the pace causes a muddled race with no one taking a clear lead and the field bunches, creating a lottery in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If early confusion over the pace causes a muddled race with no one taking a clear lead and the field bunches, creating a lottery in the final two furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Saliko's willingness to stride on alone from the front is entirely unproven — if she idles or comes back to the field before the home turn, the race could compress dramatically and alter every scenario's probability.

Rosemary May is flagged as fading in the finish; watch whether Rhys Elliott attempts to push her forward earlier than her natural style would suggest, which could cause her to stop even sooner in a Good to Firm end-to-end contest.

Phaedra runs just 8 days after her last start over the same trip — watch for any sign of jaded movement in the preliminaries or a sluggish early break that would leave Tom Kiely-Marshall needing to use more horse than intended.

Dinah Myte attempts a career-longest trip today on a surface markedly quicker than her recent wins on artificial going — if she handles Good to Firm well in the early stages, she becomes more interesting; if she races green or wide, discount immediately.

With five of six runners carrying some degree of redistribution or style-fit discount, the race map is inherently unstable — watch the first two furlongs closely to see whether any runner defies their mapped position and takes up an unexpected role that reorders the entire shape.

races.name: Last Orders Dash Handicap

runners_data.name: Balmoral Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Nigel Tinkler with form figures of 3-6-5-8-0 that include a recent run over this exact 8f trip on Good ground (11th); stepping up to 1m2f for the first time suggests connections are seeking more stamina, and the fast ground is fine, but no wins or places on similar going from 5 attempts warrants caution.

runners_data.name: Regulus Black
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, and his 2024 win at 1m2f on Good ground is directly relevant here; Hugo Palmer's trainer-14-day strike rate of 4/36 gives quiet confidence, and Ross Coakley is a capable claiming partner — the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that he's racing in a slightly more prominent role than ideal, but he is the natural pace horse in this field.

runners_data.name: Palace Artois
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner who has failed to finish in the first five in five consecutive starts, all over shorter trips of 7f-8f; this step up to 1m2f with hood (headgear noted) could unlock improvement, and the trainer's 11/58 T14 rate is healthy, but the 0-from-5 profile on similar going is a hard fact to ignore.

runners_data.name: Sound Gloria
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's lightly-raced filly has run only three times, all finishing 7th or worse; she is a natural hold-up horse by inclination but the field's surplus of closers means she is unlikely to get the wide-open, late-running scenario she would need — the 26-day gap since her last run is not a concern for this handler.

runners_data.name: Baldosa
runners_data.note: Bred and raced as a hold-up type, Baldosa has placed twice at 10f on comparable ground (2nd/STA, 4th/GOO) which makes her the most experienced closer in the field over this sort of trip; Nigel Tinkler's yard is out of form at 0/21 over 14 days, and being unable to settle into her natural rear position due to field compression is the central tactical problem.

runners_data.name: Alcanzor
runners_data.note: Carries a specific "fades in finish" flag that is a material concern at 1m2f on fast ground; Tim Easterby's yard is active (6/71 T14) but a 54-day absence and a form string of 87-0 over shorter trips makes this a speculative entry, and the redistribution away from his natural closing position compounds the risk.

runners_data.name: Enduring Story
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's runner has six career starts without a win or a place, all over 7f, and tackles 1m2f for the first time here; the step up in trip is the sole angle of improvement to grasp, though the weight of evidence — 0-from-6 record, bottom-of-the-handicap OR of 45 — suggests this is an experience-gathering run rather than a winning one.

races.paceDynamic: Regulus Black is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m2f handicap and, with no meaningful pace rival to pressurise him, he is likely to control proceedings from the outset at a measured, sustainable gallop on ground that has raced Good To Firm throughout the evening. The remainder of the field — Sound Gloria, Baldosa, Alcanzor, and Enduring Story — are all genuine hold-up types by nature but have been redistributed into midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers for the rear to accommodate; in reality, several will be jostling for the same ground and none can be certain of securing their preferred position. Balmoral Boy and Palace Artois are the only other runners likely to track Regulus Black with any purpose, giving the field a compact, processional shape through the middle stages. The tactical verdict is clear: with one horse controlling an uncontested lead at a likely honest-but-not-brutal clip over an extended mile-and-two on fast ground, genuinely prominent horses who can maintain contact and produce a decisive turn of foot in the home straight are favoured — pure hold-up horses face the additional burden of covering extra ground from wide or deep positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Regulus Black Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Regulus Black breaks cleanly and dictates a controlled, front-running display without being headed or seriously pressured.
scenarios.body: If Regulus Black breaks cleanly and dictates a controlled, front-running display without being headed or seriously pressured.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Regulus Black sets a pace that proves just fast enough to expose him in the final two furlongs, and a close-tracking horse picks him off.
scenarios.body: If Regulus Black sets a pace that proves just fast enough to expose him in the final two furlongs, and a close-tracking horse picks him off.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Through Tired Horses
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely end-to-end and the field comes back to the redistributed hold-up types in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely end-to-end and the field comes back to the redistributed hold-up types in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Competitive Affair
scenarios.trigger: If there is crowding, a slow early tempo and multiple horses attempting to assert entering the straight, creating a genuinely open finish.
scenarios.body: If there is crowding, a slow early tempo and multiple horses attempting to assert entering the straight, creating a genuinely open finish.

watchPoints.text: Regulus Black — watch whether he breaks cleanly from his stall; if he is slow away and loses the lead to Balmoral Boy or Palace Artois early, the entire pace dynamic changes and the 65% dominant scenario collapses.

Baldosa and Sound Gloria — both are true hold-up horses forced into midfield by field composition; watch whether they attempt to push forward at the start, creating an unexpectedly contested early pace that drags Regulus Black into a faster-than-ideal gallop.

Alcanzor — the "fades in finish" flag combined with a 54-day absence means connections may send him forward earlier than usual; if he sits prominently rather than from the rear, he could inject pace into the middle stages before stopping in the straight and causing traffic problems.

Palace Artois — first run in headgear (hood noted) for William Haggas; market moves in the final 20 minutes before post time are worth monitoring as this is exactly the kind of handler who fits horses with gear for specific tactical reasons.

Going — all evening races at Nottingham have been Good To Firm despite the declared Good; horses with Good To Firm form hold an edge, and the faster surface marginally increases the likelihood of Regulus Black's front-running lead proving decisive.

races.name: Construction Day 14th October Handicap

runners_data.name: Didaar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with modest recent form (983-67) but a third over 8f on good ground is the most relevant form line; headgear (hood/p) suggests needs settling, and a 14-day return for a low-profile trainer is neutral — should travel kindly in midfield off this pace and is one of the more natural closers in the field.

runners_data.name: Holly Mist
runners_data.note: Unclassified style suggests tactical flexibility; Roger Varian's record of 9/32 T14 is solid, and the horse has posted placed efforts over 8-12f on soft and standard — the good-to-firm conditions here are a query given all recent runs came on softer surfaces, making the going the key risk factor.

runners_data.name: Time Turner
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who won over 12f on standard and was placed over 10f on the same surface; this trip and fast ground are appropriate, and Edward Bethell's 5/30 T14 keeps him in the picture — the headgear (visor) suggests he needs a strong pace to get competitive but may adapt if he can track closer.

runners_data.name: Stipulation
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and pace-setter for this race; wins from this position (1W) in similar conditions are on record, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) notes he is arguably racing out of his optimal role — his chance relies entirely on dominating from the front unchallenged, and Mark Loughnane's 0/17 T14 offers no recent encouragement.

runners_data.name: Into Combat
runners_data.note: A natural deep hold-up type with a fade-in-finish warning and a string of poor efforts (6780-0) that make the form unappealing; Sir Mark Prescott runners at this trip should always be respected, but the redistribution to midfield masks his true trailing nature and the recent record is hard to overcome.

runners_data.name: Danehill Star
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's runner brings the best recent form among the hold-up group (221433) with five placed efforts in similar conditions including a win over 10f on standard; genuinely placed on good ground (7 runs), he is the most likely of the remapped closers to push forward and secure a viable racing position — his consistency makes him hard to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Pride Eye
runners_data.note: Carries a fade-in-finish flag and all career runs have been on standard ground, making this good-to-firm surface a significant unknown; 124 days off the track adds further uncertainty, and while a win over 8f on standard is on record, the combination of going concern, fitness question and redistribution from his natural rear position makes him the hardest to trust.

runners_data.name: Quirke On Parole
runners_data.note: Lightly raced over 8-10f with a win (1W) on good ground but otherwise uninspiring efforts (57-097); Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim could trim the weight advantage slightly, but consistent finishing positions of 7th-10th in similar fields mean his natural position deep in the field, where he has been remapped from, is unlikely to produce a winning effort here.

races.paceDynamic: Stipulation is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine challenger pressing from the outside, is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this flat Nottingham mile-and-two-furlongs on good-to-firm ground. The pace will be honest but unspectacular — Stipulation is unlikely to be wound up early, meaning the race will be run at an even tempo that compresses the field and limits the swing in fortunes between sections. Behind the leader, a cluster of hold-up types — Didaar, Time Turner, Holly Mist and others — will track through the middle portion of the race, setting up a straight-line dash from the home turn. This shape is tailor-made for a prominent-tracking or progressive hold-up horse with a clean turn of foot, as the lack of genuine pace pressure means late closers need genuine acceleration rather than just stamina. Several runners including Into Combat, Danehill Star, Pride Eye and Quirke On Parole are true hold-up horses remapped to midfield because the field holds more deep closers than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — of those, Danehill Star and Didaar are most likely to secure a forward position closer to where they are shown.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stipulation Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Stipulation is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a steady-to-fair gallop that suits a hold-up horse with a mid-race kick.
scenarios.body: If Stipulation is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a steady-to-fair gallop that suits a hold-up horse with a mid-race kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Catch A Lone Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Stipulation's lone-lead advantage is eroded on the testing ground-to-firm conditions and more-effective hold-up horses pounce late.
scenarios.body: If Stipulation's lone-lead advantage is eroded on the testing ground-to-firm conditions and more-effective hold-up horses pounce late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking Stipulation in second or third place travels powerfully throughout and strikes as soon as the home turn is reached.
scenarios.body: If a horse tracking Stipulation in second or third place travels powerfully throughout and strikes as soon as the home turn is reached.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Compressed Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the even gallop produces a bunched, muddling finish with multiple horses challenging simultaneously in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the even gallop produces a bunched, muddling finish with multiple horses challenging simultaneously in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Danehill Star (Tony Carroll) — if he pushes forward from his mapped midfield position to track Stipulation early, he becomes the most dangerous horse in the race given his consistency on this type of going and at this trip.

Stipulation's gallop fractions — if he is allowed to set a very slow pace, the entire field will be in contention turning for home, neutralising his front-running advantage and opening the door for anything with a turn of foot.
